_about: Factory settings: the one place for their values (core/settings.js reads them). This file holds the shared defaults and is tracked by Git. Personal changes go to settings/local.json next to it (ignored by Git; the editor's settings write it): the same structure, only the keys that change; objects merge key by key, other values replace. An empty object here is an open map, and so is an object marked "_open": true: any keys may be added under it. The API key is never here. provider.use: which image provider generates, "openrouter" or "codex-cli". provider.openrouter (core/providers/openrouter.js): OpenRouter-compatible endpoint, model id, fallbackModel = the model tried in the same attempt when the main one fails (an error, a refusal, an answer without an image; null = none), aspectRatio = the ratio wanted for a card (the model is asked for the ratio of its profile closest to it, and the card is cut from the answer: core/image/prepare.js), keyEnvVar = the environment variable (or the line of .env in the project root) that holds the key, params = any other request fields passed as is to every model (a model's own profile params are added over them), timeout per call in ms, retries on HTTP 429/5xx and the backoff before the first retry in ms. provider.models (core/providers/models.js): the profile of each image model, keyed by its id ("codex-cli" for Codex), an open map ("_open": a profile for any model may be added): aspectRatios = the ratios it accepts (null = any, said in words), maxReferences = input images one request may carry (more is refused before anything is sent), params = request fields this model needs, prompt = how its provider advises writing prompts, source = where these facts come from and when they were checked; a model without a profile is asked for 1:1 with no extra fields. provider.codexCli (core/providers/codex-cli.js; Codex's own login, no per-image payment): the command, the orchestrating model (null = the user's Codex config), the aspect ratio said in the brief, timeout in ms, reasoning effort, sandbox, and the prompt template ({refs} = legend of attached images, {brief} = the card prompt). card: attempts = how many generations of one card one `card make` run may spend at most; maxSpendUsd = the spend cap of one run in USD, checked before every paid call. editPrompt = the whole prompt of `card edit` ({wish}), sent with the card's model image as the input image; editLegend = how Codex is told what the attached image is. tuneProcessing = after each generation search the post-processing settings per card (core/card/tune.js, bounds in styles/<style>/processing.json); false = apply the starting settings as they are. processing: post-processing settings per model (core/image/adjust.js settings object; the key is the OpenRouter model id, or "codex-cli"), only to override the style's own starting settings (styles/<style>/processing.json → start). vision: the vision model that looks at finished cards, asked through provider.openrouter (its endpoint and key): model id, format = the answer convention of its family (a key of FORMATS in core/card/hero.js), reasoning = the request's reasoning field as is (null = not sent; this model refuses reasoning turned off and takes the efforts low, medium and high), timeout per call in ms. hero (core/card/hero.js): finding the hero's outline for the checks when no agent or person gives its box — the vision model gives the box and the outline is cut inside it; mirrorCheck = ask also on the mirror image of the card and trust the outline only when the two boxes overlap at least agreeIou (intersection over union); maxTokens per answer (the model's reasoning counts in it: 400 cut the answers of gemini-3.8-flash); prompt.template with {width} {height} {hero} {answer}, and the hero's words for an object card or a scene ({what} = the order's subject, object or scene). look (core/card/look.js): the vision model looks at every attempt, when a key is there, and says whether the picture is what the order asked for and holds nothing unordered; use = on or off (an agent that looks at every card itself may turn it off), maxTokens per answer, blocking = the order questions whose "no" makes the loop regenerate (the other questions and the style's checklist for eyes go to the report; caption is not blocking: a caption that does not name the subject is usually the plan's error, which a new picture does not fix), prompt: template ({title} = the caption, {order} = the assembled prompt without its note on reference images, {questions}, {checklist} = the style's checklist for eyes of the attempt, {answer}), wish ({wish} = the person's words of the attempt), questions (the key names the kind of problem), answer ({json} = the answer's shape, built from the question keys). set (core/set): parallel = cards of one set made at the same time; maxSpendUsd = the spend cap of one set's cards in USD (each card also keeps card.maxSpendUsd). set.plan: the text model that writes set plans when no agent does (the editor's path), asked through provider.openrouter (its endpoint and key): model id, repairs = how many times the plan's rule errors are sent back to the model for a fix, maxTokens and temperature per answer, reasoning = the request's reasoning field as is (null = not sent), timeout per call in ms, maxSpendUsd = the spend cap of one planning run (a set with its variants, or a whole collection) in USD. text.help (core/text/draft.js): the editor's text help, which turns a producer's rough notes in a free-text field into the finished text with the text model of set.plan (its model, reasoning and timeout): maxTokens per answer (the bound of one call's price) and temperature; template ({what} {form} {context} {notes}); kinds = one entry per field it serves (what the text is, its form); contextLead = the line before what the text belongs to; context = how each piece of it is said ({value}). editor (editor/server.mjs): port = the local port the editor listens on (when taken, a free one is used); openBrowser = open the browser when the editor starts.

google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1.prompt: Google: describe the scene as a narrative paragraph, not a keyword list (subject, action, setting, composition, style); say what is wanted, not what is not ("an empty street", not "no cars"); name placement and empty space in words; say what each attached image is for and how it relates to the new image.
google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1.source: openrouter.ai/google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1 (aspect_ratio list, "an unlisted value is rejected"; input_references up to 14; resolution 1K | 2K | 4K; n = 1), checked 2026-10-30; prompting: cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana and ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation

openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare.prompt: OpenAI: a consistent order — scene, subject, key details, constraints; short labelled segments read better than one long paragraph; name materials, light, colours and the medium; give each input image a number and a role; short exclusions such as "no extra text, no watermark" are allowed at the end.
openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare.source: openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare (aspect_ratio list, no resolution field, quality auto | low | medium | high | xhigh | max, input_references up to 16), checked 2026-10-30; prompting: developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-prompting

codex-cli.prompt: Codex draws with OpenAI's image tool: as for GPT Image; the ratio is said in words in the brief.
codex-cli.source: core/providers/codex-cli.js: at most 5 -i images work in Codex's image tool (codex-cli 0.166.0)

card.editPrompt: Edit the attached image: {wish} Keep everything this does not ask to change exactly as it is: the subject, the composition, the backdrop, the colours and the rendering style. Return the whole edited image.
card.editLegend: The attached image is the card to edit; change only what the brief asks.

prompt.template: This is a {width} x {height} px card illustration. Find {hero}. Give the tightest box around all of it: include every thin part (tips, antennas, handles, rings, things sticking out of it or held by it). Exclude the backdrop, any glow or light halo behind it, its cast shadow, and the floor, table, ground or surface patch it stands on. {answer}
prompt.scene: the characters together with the props they hold or act with (the hero of this scene: «{what}»)

questions.subject: Is the main subject the kind of thing the order describes, with the parts the order names (a kettle drawn when a teapot was ordered → false; a bench drawn when a pier was ordered → false)? A part or a detail drawn a little differently (a shade of colour, a strap, how a surface is finished) is a difference to list, not a false.
questions.caption: Would a viewer who sees only the picture name its main subject with the caption's words (the caption «Lantern» under a drawn candle → false)?
questions.staging: Are the backdrop, the support and the setting the kinds the order describes, in the colours the order names for them (a brick wall ordered but a plain gradient drawn → false; a mint green wall ordered but a yellow wall drawn → false; a floor, a patch of real surface or a landscape where the order asks for one)? How high a floor or a surface reaches, the margins and the sizes are measured by the program: list them as differences, but do not answer false for them.
questions.additions: Is the image free of things that do not belong: a face on fish, animals or objects that are not the ordered characters (a mouth, a smile, brows, an expression; simple natural eyes on a fish or an animal are fine, eyes on an object are not); a creature or a character the order does not have; text, letters or numbers; a frame or a caption plate? In a scene, props of the scene's activity and of its place are fine.
questions.costume: If the order has characters: does each one wear every costume item the order names (ok = null when there are no characters)?

prompt.answer: Answer only compact JSON on one line: {json}. First write "seen": the main subject as a viewer would name it, in a few words; then "differences": every visible way the picture differs from the order — a thing, part, costume item, backdrop or support missing or different, something added — as short phrases, an empty list when there are none; then judge the questions from them. "why" says what is wrong when ok is false and is empty otherwise. "checklist" lists only the items that do not hold, with the id as written; an empty list when all hold.

collection.what: the description of a card collection: what it is about, its mood and who it is for; every set of the collection is planned from it
collection.form: One paragraph of three to six plain sentences.

setTheme.what: the theme of one set of ten cards: what the set is about
setTheme.form: A few words on one line, like a short title.

wishes.what: the producer's wishes for a set or a whole collection of cards: what to show, what to avoid, the mood
wishes.form: One wish per line, each a short plain sentence.

cardWish.what: a wish to change one finished card illustration: what to change in the picture
cardWish.form: One or two sentences of concrete visual instructions about the picture.

cardsTheme.what: the theme of a few loose cards: what they show
cardsTheme.form: A few words on one line.

help.contextLead: What the text belongs to, for your understanding only: never repeat it in the text unless the notes say it.
